functions.name: isofs_Init
functions.description: Initializes the ISO filesystem layer for accessing files within an ISO image. Expected usage: call once before any other isofs_* function to set the active ISO image given by iso_path. The isBigEndian flag likely indicates endianness handling for the target environment (e.g., PS2), but exact effects are not documented. Returns a 64-bit value (purpose and error convention not explicitly documented; likely related to image size or a status code).
requirements: Must be called before isofs_Open, isofs_Read, isofs_Seek, isofs_Close, and isofs_ReadISO.
iso_path must point to an existing, readable ISO image file path.
isBigEndian is expected to be a boolean-like flag (0 or 1); exact accepted range is not documented.
Caller must check the return value for success/failure; exact error convention is not documented.
Not documented whether repeated initialization is allowed without isofs_Reset; if reinitializing, call isofs_Reset first (inferred; details unknown).

functions.name: isofs_Reset
functions.description: Resets the ISO filesystem layer, releasing internal state/resources associated with a previously initialized ISO image. Expected usage: call to deinitialize or reinitialize the system between ISO images.
requirements: Should only be called after a prior successful isofs_Init (inferred from purpose).
After reset, any previously obtained file descriptors from isofs_Open should be considered invalid (inferred; exact behavior not documented).
Caller must check the return value for success/failure; exact error convention is not documented.

functions.name: isofs_Open
functions.description: Opens a file inside the currently initialized ISO image and returns a file descriptor-like integer handle for subsequent operations. Expected usage: call after isofs_Init to obtain a handle to a file path within the ISO’s directory tree.
requirements: isofs_Init must have been successfully called prior to opening files.
filename must refer to a valid path within the mounted ISO image; it must follow the ISO’s path/filename conventions.
The returned integer handle must be preserved and later passed to isofs_Read, isofs_Seek, and isofs_Close.
Caller must check the return value for success/failure; exact error convention is not documented.

functions.name: isofs_Close
functions.description: Closes a previously opened file descriptor associated with a file inside the ISO image. Expected usage: call when finished with a handle returned by isofs_Open.
requirements: fd must be a valid descriptor previously returned by isofs_Open and not yet closed.
After a successful close, fd must not be used again.
Caller must check the return value for success/failure; exact error convention is not documented.

functions.name: isofs_Read
functions.signature: int isofs_Read(int fd, void *buf, u32 nbytes);
functions.description: Reads up to nbytes of data from an open file within the ISO image into the provided buffer. Expected usage: use with a valid descriptor from isofs_Open; supports iterative reads to stream file contents.
requirements: fd must be a valid descriptor returned by isofs_Open and not yet closed.
buf must be a non-null pointer to writable memory of at least nbytes bytes.
nbytes specifies the number of bytes to read; behavior for zero is unspecified (likely a no-op).
The current file position is advanced by the number of bytes actually read; exact semantics for EOF/partial reads are not documented.
Caller must check the return value for success/failure and number of bytes read; exact error convention is not documented.

functions.name: isofs_Seek
functions.signature: int isofs_Seek(int fd, u32 offset, int origin);
functions.description: Changes the file position for an open file within the ISO image. Expected usage: reposition before reading using standard origin semantics similar to lseek/fseek.
requirements: fd must be a valid descriptor returned by isofs_Open and not yet closed.
origin should be one of the standard constants (e.g., SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR, SEEK_END); exact accepted values are not documented here.
offset is interpreted relative to origin; valid range and behavior when seeking beyond file bounds are not documented.
Caller must check the return value for success/failure; exact error convention is not documented.

functions.name: isofs_ReadISO
functions.signature: int isofs_ReadISO(s64 offset, u32 nbytes, void *buf);
functions.description: Performs a raw read directly from the ISO image at the given byte offset, bypassing file descriptors. Expected usage: read arbitrary sectors/bytes from the ISO data for low-level operations or metadata parsing.
requirements: isofs_Init must have been successfully called; an ISO image must be loaded.
buf must be a non-null pointer to writable memory of at least nbytes bytes.
offset is a byte offset from the start of the ISO image; valid range is not documented here.
nbytes is the number of bytes to read; behavior for zero is unspecified (likely a no-op).
Caller must check the return value for success/failure and number of bytes read; exact error convention is not documented.
